seoTitle: Free jq Playground - Test jq Filters Online
metaDescription: Run jq filters on your JSON in the browser: select, map, group_by, sort_by, reduce, string interpolation and @csv. A jq subset, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Paste JSON, write a jq filter, and see every result the way the jq command line prints it. Useful for drafting a filter before it goes into a shell script or CI step.
why:
jq is the standard way to slice JSON on the command line, but getting a filter right usually means retyping it in a terminal over and over. Here you can edit the filter beside the data and see each output immediately, with compact, raw and sorted-key switches that mirror the -c, -r and -S flags.

This is a subset of jq 1.7 written for the browser: paths, pipes, comma, select, map, sort_by, group_by, unique_by, min_by, reduce, if/elif/else, variables with as, string interpolation, the @csv, @tsv, @json, @base64 and @uri formats, regex tests and about ninety built-ins. It does not implement assignment operators (|=, +=), def, del or path functions, so a filter that needs those will report that clearly. Results were checked against the real jq on more than 150 filters. Everything runs locally and the JSON never leaves the page.
howTo: Paste your JSON into the first box.
Type a jq filter in the second box, for example .items[] | select(.price > 10) | .name.
Tick Raw output to drop the quotes around strings, Compact for one line per result, Sort keys to order object keys.

faq.a: No. It is a JavaScript implementation of the commonly used part of jq 1.7. Common filters give identical output to the real tool, but assignments (|=), def, del, paths and limits such as arbitrary precision for huge integers are not supported.

faq.q: Why does my filter print several results?
faq.a: jq filters are generators. A filter such as .items[] emits one result per element, and each is printed separately, exactly as on the command line. Wrap the filter in [ ... ] to collect the results into one array.

faq.q: Can I process several JSON documents at once?
faq.a: If the input is several JSON values one after another, the filter runs on each. Tick Slurp to wrap them in a single array first, like jq -s.
No. The filter and JSON are processed in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
